report_name: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard Exposed in Third-Party Vendor Breach

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Threat Actor
threat_actors.description: The unidentified threat actors responsible for the supply chain compromise of a vendor to JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard. This entity is a placeholder for the unknown group that conducted the attack.

attack_patterns.name: Supply Chain Compromise
attack_patterns.description: The incident is described as a classic supply chain attack, where attackers targeted larger organizations (JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard) by compromising a shared, less secure third-party vendor.

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: The breach occurred due to the compromise of a trusted relationship between the financial firms and their third-party vendor, which had been granted access to their data.

identities.name: JPMorgan
identities.description: A financial services firm whose customer data was compromised due to a security breach at a shared third-party vendor.

identities.name: Visa
identities.description: A financial services corporation whose customer data was compromised due to a security breach at a shared third-party vendor.

identities.name: Mastercard
identities.description: A financial services corporation whose customer data was compromised due to a security breach at a shared third-party vendor.

indicators.name: Anomalous M365 File Access by Guest User
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous M365 File Access by Guest User
id: 2b1f8e3c-9d7a-4b0f-8c1d-5a6b7c8d9e0f
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects a high volume of file access events in Microsoft 365 (SharePoint) by a single guest user account.
  This could indicate a compromised third-party account being used for data reconnaissance or collection as part of a supply chain attack.
references:
  - https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-23
tags:
  - attack.t1195
  - attack.t1199
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.sharepoint
level: medium
detection:
  selection:
    Operation: FileAccessed
    UserId|contains: '#EXT#@'
  condition: selection | count(UserId) > 100 by UserId
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate high-volume activity by a guest user or third-party application.
  - Threshold may need to be adjusted based on environment baselines.
indicators.description: Detects a high volume of file access events in Microsoft 365 by a single guest user, which could indicate a compromised third-party account being used for data collection, as suggested in the hunting hints.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous M365 File Access by Guest User
